title: Naval Topic 8 生词 · 英英解释

items.ex: Fame is when a lot of people know who you are. Famous people have fame.

src.t: Is fame a worthwhile goal?
src.zh: 名气是个值得追求的目标吗？

items.ex: To invite someone means to ask them to come to an event or a place.
exs: She invited me to her birthday party.

src.t: It gets you invited to better parties. It gets you to better restaurants.
src.zh: 它能让你被邀请去更好的派对，能让你进更好的餐厅。

items.ex: A pedestal is a base that a statue stands on. To put someone on a pedestal means to treat them as if they are perfect and better than others.
exs: Don't put your idols on a pedestal.
Fans put celebrities on a pedestal.

src.t: Fame is this funny thing where a lot of people know you, but you don’t know them, and it does get you put on the pedestal.
src.zh: 名气是个很奇怪的东西：很多人认识你，你却不认识他们，而且它确实会把你捧上神坛。

items.ex: At distance, or at a distance, means from far away, without being close or meeting in person.
exs: You can get things done at a distance with your phone.
I watched the show at a distance.

src.t: It can get you what you want at distance, so I wouldn’t say it’s worthless.
src.zh: 它能让你隔着老远就得到想要的东西，所以我不会说它一文不值。

items.ex: Worthless means it has no value. It is useless or not worth anything.

src.t: It can get you what you want at distance, so I wouldn’t say it’s worthless.
src.zh: 它能让你隔着老远就得到想要的东西，所以我不会说它一文不值。

items.ex: Obviously means it is easy to see or understand. Everybody knows it.
exs: Obviously, I want my clients to be happy.

src.t: Obviously people want it for a reason, it’s high status so it attracts the opposite sex, especially for men it attracts women.
src.zh: 显然人们想要它是有原因的：它代表高地位，所以能吸引异性，尤其对男人来说，它能吸引女人。

items.ex: Status is your position in a group, how important other people think you are.
exs: A big house can be a status symbol.

src.t: Obviously people want it for a reason, it’s high status so it attracts the opposite sex, especially for men it attracts women.
src.zh: 显然人们想要它是有原因的：它代表高地位，所以能吸引异性，尤其对男人来说，它能吸引女人。

items.ex: To attract means to pull someone or something toward you, to make people interested.

src.t: Obviously people want it for a reason, it’s high status so it attracts the opposite sex, especially for men it attracts women.
src.zh: 显然人们想要它是有原因的：它代表高地位，所以能吸引异性，尤其对男人来说，它能吸引女人。

items.ex: The opposite sex means people of the other gender. For a man, it is women. For a woman, it is men.
exs: He's shy around the opposite sex.

src.t: Obviously people want it for a reason, it’s high status so it attracts the opposite sex, especially for men it attracts women.
src.zh: 显然人们想要它是有原因的：它代表高地位，所以能吸引异性，尤其对男人来说，它能吸引女人。

items.ex: Privacy is being free from other people watching you or knowing about your life.

src.t: That said, it is high cost. It means you have no privacy, you do have weirdos and lunatics,
src.ft: That said, it is high cost. It means you have no privacy, you do have weirdos and lunatics, you do get hit up a lot for weird things, and you’re on a stage so you’re forced to perform.
src.zh: 话虽如此，它的代价也很高。它意味着你没有隐私，你确实会碰到怪人和疯子，你确实会经常因为一些奇怪的事被人找上门，而且你站在舞台上，就不得不一直表演。

items.ex: A weirdo is a person who acts strangely, in a way that can make you uncomfortable. It is a casual, not very nice word.
exs: Some weirdo kept calling the salon.

src.t: That said, it is high cost. It means you have no privacy, you do have weirdos and lunatics,
src.ft: That said, it is high cost. It means you have no privacy, you do have weirdos and lunatics, you do get hit up a lot for weird things, and you’re on a stage so you’re forced to perform.
src.zh: 话虽如此，它的代价也很高。它意味着你没有隐私，你确实会碰到怪人和疯子，你确实会经常因为一些奇怪的事被人找上门，而且你站在舞台上，就不得不一直表演。

items.ex: A lunatic is a person who acts in a crazy or dangerous way. It is a strong, informal word.

src.t: That said, it is high cost. It means you have no privacy, you do have weirdos and lunatics,
src.ft: That said, it is high cost. It means you have no privacy, you do have weirdos and lunatics, you do get hit up a lot for weird things, and you’re on a stage so you’re forced to perform.
src.zh: 话虽如此，它的代价也很高。它意味着你没有隐私，你确实会碰到怪人和疯子，你确实会经常因为一些奇怪的事被人找上门，而且你站在舞台上，就不得不一直表演。

items.ex: To hit someone up means to contact them, often to ask for something. Famous people get hit up a lot.
exs: Hit me up if you need an appointment.
He hit me up for money again.

src.t: you do get hit up a lot for weird things, and you’re on a stage so you’re forced to perform.
src.ft: That said, it is high cost. It means you have no privacy, you do have weirdos and lunatics, you do get hit up a lot for weird things, and you’re on a stage so you’re forced to perform.
src.zh: 话虽如此，它的代价也很高。它意味着你没有隐私，你确实会碰到怪人和疯子，你确实会经常因为一些奇怪的事被人找上门，而且你站在舞台上，就不得不一直表演。

items.ex: To perform means to act, sing or do something in front of people. It can also mean to act in a way people expect.
exs: She performs on stage every weekend.
I feel I have to perform for my followers.

src.t: you do get hit up a lot for weird things, and you’re on a stage so you’re forced to perform.
src.ft: That said, it is high cost. It means you have no privacy, you do have weirdos and lunatics, you do get hit up a lot for weird things, and you’re on a stage so you’re forced to perform.
src.zh: 话虽如此，它的代价也很高。它意味着你没有隐私，你确实会碰到怪人和疯子，你确实会经常因为一些奇怪的事被人找上门，而且你站在舞台上，就不得不一直表演。

items.ex: Consistent means always the same, not changing. If your actions are consistent with your words, they match.
exs: Be consistent with your lash mapping.

src.t: You’re forced to be consistent with your past proclamations and actions, and you’re gonna have haters and all that nonsense.
src.zh: 你不得不和自己过去公开说过的话、做过的事保持一致，你还会有黑粉，以及各种乱七八糟的事。

items.ex: A proclamation is a public and official statement. Naval means big public statements you made in the past.
exs: Be careful with loud public proclamations.

src.t: You’re forced to be consistent with your past proclamations and actions, and you’re gonna have haters and all that nonsense.
src.zh: 你不得不和自己过去公开说过的话、做过的事保持一致，你还会有黑粉，以及各种乱七八糟的事。

items.ex: A hater is a person who always says bad things about someone, often because they are jealous.

src.t: You’re forced to be consistent with your past proclamations and actions, and you’re gonna have haters and all that nonsense.
src.zh: 你不得不和自己过去公开说过的话、做过的事保持一致，你还会有黑粉，以及各种乱七八糟的事。

items.ex: Nonsense is something silly that does not make sense or is not important.
exs: I don't have time for this nonsense.

src.t: You’re forced to be consistent with your past proclamations and actions, and you’re gonna have haters and all that nonsense.
src.zh: 你不得不和自己过去公开说过的话、做过的事保持一致，你还会有黑粉，以及各种乱七八糟的事。

items.ex: Disingenuous means not honest or sincere. You pretend to believe something, but you don't really.
exs: It's disingenuous to say money doesn't matter.

src.t: But the fact that we do it, the fact that we all seem to want it means that it would be disingenuous to say, “Oh no, no, I’m famous, but you don’t wanna be.”
src.zh: 但我们确实在做这件事，我们好像都想要它，这就说明，如果说“哦不不，我是出名了，但你不会想出名的”，那就太不真诚了。

items.ex: A byproduct is something that comes naturally from doing something else. You did not aim for it directly.
exs: Happiness is a byproduct of a good life.
Fame should be a byproduct of good work.

src.t: That said, I think fame, like anything else, is best produced as a byproduct of something potentially more worthwhile.
src.zh: 话虽如此，我觉得名气和其他东西一样，最好是作为某件可能更有价值的事情的副产品出现。

items.ex: Potentially means it is possible, it could happen or could be true in the future.
exs: This could potentially save you time.

src.t: That said, I think fame, like anything else, is best produced as a byproduct of something potentially more worthwhile.
src.zh: 话虽如此，我觉得名气和其他东西一样，最好是作为某件可能更有价值的事情的副产品出现。

items.ex: To crave means to want something very strongly, almost like you need it.

src.t: Wanting to be famous and craving to be famous and being famous for being famous, these are sort of traps.
src.zh: 想出名、渴望出名、因为出名而出名，这些都算是陷阱。

items.ex: A trap is something that catches you. Once you are in it, it is hard to get out.
exs: Social media can be a trap.

src.t: Wanting to be famous and craving to be famous and being famous for being famous, these are sort of traps.
src.zh: 想出名、渴望出名、因为出名而出名，这些都算是陷阱。

items.ex: For something's sake means doing it only for that thing itself, with no other reason. Fame for fame's sake is fame with no real purpose behind it.
exs: Don't change the menu just for change's sake.
He loves to argue for argument's sake.

src.t: Fame for fame’s sake.
src.zh: 为了出名而出名。

exzh: 别只是为了改变而改变菜单。
他就喜欢为了争论而争论。

items.ex: Exactly means correct in every way. People also say Exactly! to agree strongly.

src.t: Yeah exactly, so it’s better that it’s earned fame.
src.zh: 对，没错，所以最好是挣来的名气。

items.ex: A tribe is a group of people who live together and share the same culture. Today it can mean your group or community.
exs: My lash community feels like a tribe.

src.t: For example, earned respect in the tribe is you do things that are good for the tribe.
src.zh: 比如说，在部落里挣来的尊重，就是你做了对部落有益的事。

items.ex: To transcend means to go beyond the normal limits of something. To transcend the self means to think beyond only yourself.

src.t: Who are the most famous people in human history? There are people who sort of transcended the self, the Buddhas and the Jesuses and the Mohammads of the world.
src.zh: 人类历史上最有名的人是谁？是那些某种程度上超越了自我的人，像佛陀、耶稣、穆罕默德这些人。

items.ex: To discover means to find something for the first time, something nobody knew before.
exs: Scientists discover new things every day.
I discovered a great lash supplier.

src.t: Who else is famous? The artists are famous—art lasts for a long time. The scientists are famous—they discover things.
src.zh: 还有谁出名？艺术家出名——艺术能流传很久。科学家出名——他们发现新东西。

items.ex: Presumably means you think it is probably true, but you are not completely sure.
exs: She's late, presumably because of traffic.
Presumably, he knows what he's doing.

src.t: The conquerors are famous, presumably because they conquered for their tribe, was someone that they were fighting for.
src.zh: 征服者出名，大概是因为他们是为自己的部落去征服的，是在为某些人而战。

items.ex: Tyrannical means using power in a cruel and unfair way, like a tyrant, a bad ruler.

src.t: So generally the higher up you rise by doing things for greater and greater groups of people, even though it may be considered tyrannical or negative,
src.ft: So generally the higher up you rise by doing things for greater and greater groups of people, even though it may be considered tyrannical or negative, like Genghis Khan is famous, but to the Mongols he was doing good, to the rest of them not so much.
src.zh: 所以总的来说，你为越来越大的人群做事，你就爬得越高，哪怕这些事可能被认为是专横的、负面的，比如成吉思汗很有名，对蒙古人来说他在做好事，对其他人来说就没那么好了。

items.ex: Not so much is a casual way to say not really, or not very much, often in contrast to something before.
exs: I love coffee. Tea, not so much.
To him it was great, to others not so much.

src.t: like Genghis Khan is famous, but to the Mongols he was doing good, to the rest of them not so much.
src.ft: So generally the higher up you rise by doing things for greater and greater groups of people, even though it may be considered tyrannical or negative, like Genghis Khan is famous, but to the Mongols he was doing good, to the rest of them not so much.
src.zh: 所以总的来说，你为越来越大的人群做事，你就爬得越高，哪怕这些事可能被认为是专横的、负面的，比如成吉思汗很有名，对蒙古人来说他在做好事，对其他人来说就没那么好了。

items.ex: To take care of someone means to look after them and keep them safe and well. To take care of something means to deal with it.
exs: I take care of my clients' natural lashes.
Don't worry, I'll take care of it.

src.t: The higher level you’re operating at, the more people you’re taking care of, the more you sort of earn respect and fame, and I think those are good reasons to be famous.
src.zh: 你运作的层级越高，你照顾的人越多，你就越能挣得尊重和名气，我觉得这些都是出名的好理由。

items.ex: Hollow means empty inside. A hollow feeling or hollow fame has no real value inside.

src.t: If fame is empty, if you’re famous just because your name showed up in a lot of places or your face showed up in a lot of places, then that’s a hollow fame
src.ft: If fame is empty, if you’re famous just because your name showed up in a lot of places or your face showed up in a lot of places, then that’s a hollow fame and I think deep down you will know that and so it’ll be fragile and you’ll always be afraid of losing it and then you’ll be forced to perform.
src.zh: 如果名气是空的，如果你出名只是因为你的名字或者你的脸在很多地方出现过，那就是一种空洞的名气，而且我觉得你内心深处会知道这一点，所以它会很脆弱，你会一直害怕失去它，然后你就不得不一直表演。

items.ex: Deep down means in your true feelings, even if you don't show it or say it.
exs: Deep down, she knew he was right.
Deep down, I'm a shy person.

src.t: and I think deep down you will know that and so it’ll be fragile and you’ll always be afraid of losing it and then you’ll be forced to perform.
src.ft: If fame is empty, if you’re famous just because your name showed up in a lot of places or your face showed up in a lot of places, then that’s a hollow fame and I think deep down you will know that and so it’ll be fragile and you’ll always be afraid of losing it and then you’ll be forced to perform.
src.zh: 如果名气是空的，如果你出名只是因为你的名字或者你的脸在很多地方出现过，那就是一种空洞的名气，而且我觉得你内心深处会知道这一点，所以它会很脆弱，你会一直害怕失去它，然后你就不得不一直表演。

items.ex: Fragile means easy to break or damage. It can be a thing, a feeling or a situation.

src.t: and I think deep down you will know that and so it’ll be fragile and you’ll always be afraid of losing it and then you’ll be forced to perform.
src.ft: If fame is empty, if you’re famous just because your name showed up in a lot of places or your face showed up in a lot of places, then that’s a hollow fame and I think deep down you will know that and so it’ll be fragile and you’ll always be afraid of losing it and then you’ll be forced to perform.
src.zh: 如果名气是空的，如果你出名只是因为你的名字或者你的脸在很多地方出现过，那就是一种空洞的名气，而且我觉得你内心深处会知道这一点，所以它会很脆弱，你会一直害怕失去它，然后你就不得不一直表演。

items.ex: A celebrity is a famous person, especially in movies, music or TV.
exs: A celebrity came to our salon!

src.t: So the kind of fame that pure actors and celebrities have, I wouldn’t want, but the kind of fame that’s earned because you did something useful, why dodge that?
src.zh: 所以，纯演员和明星那种名气，我不想要；但如果是因为你做了有用的事而挣来的名气，为什么要躲开呢？

items.ex: To dodge means to move quickly to avoid something, or to avoid doing something you don't want to do.

src.t: So the kind of fame that pure actors and celebrities have, I wouldn’t want, but the kind of fame that’s earned because you did something useful, why dodge that?
src.zh: 所以，纯演员和明星那种名气，我不想要；但如果是因为你做了有用的事而挣来的名气，为什么要躲开呢？
